section: 01 - Foreword
rule_text: DME, prosthetic/orthotic devices (except customized devices in a SNF), supplies, and oxygen furnished during a Part A-covered hospital or SNF inpatient stay are included in the inpatient PPS payment and are not separately billable.

section: 01 - Foreword
rule_text: Only hospitals, CAHs, SNFs, and HHAs among the listed provider types generally bill DMEPOS; hospitals, CAHs, and SNFs usually bill only for outpatients. Exceptions are addressed elsewhere in the chapter.

section: 01 - Foreword
rule_text: A DMEPOS supplier must meet enrollment requirements described in the Program Integrity Manual. A provider that enrolls as a supplier is treated as a supplier for DMEPOS billing, but separate payment remains limited to items not included in a PPS rate.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2023, providers and suppliers do not submit CMNs or DIFs with claims; claims received with those forms attached are rejected and returned. For dates of service before January 1, 2023, required CMNs or DIFs must still be submitted or already on file.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: SNFs, CORFs, OPTs, and hospitals bill the A/B MAC Part A for prosthetic/orthotic devices, supplies, and covered outpatient DME and oxygen. HHAs bill DME to the A/B MAC (HHH) or may qualify as DME suppliers and bill the DME MAC.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: Unless Part A billing is specifically required, implanted DME, implanted prosthetic devices, and their replacement parts, accessories, and supplies are billed to the A/B MAC Part B rather than the DME MAC.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: A DMEPOS supplier enrolled with the NSC should enroll with and bill the A/B MAC Part B for replacement parts, accessories, and supplies for prosthetic implants and surgically implanted DME items, unless it separately qualifies for another benefit category.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: A DMEPOS supplier enrolled with the NSC bills the A/B MAC Part B using its NPI and must not include its NSC number on the claim.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: A DMEPOS supplier that did not implant an implanted device must not bill Part B for the implanted device itself, but may bill for replacement parts, accessories, and supplies for prosthetic implants and surgically implanted DME.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: Claims filing jurisdiction for these items is determined by the supplier's location, while payment for DMEPOS is based on the fee schedule amount for the state of the beneficiary's permanent residence.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: HCPCS codes for the relevant service categories are updated quarterly. New HCPCS codes not included in the DME MAC jurisdiction spreadsheet are under A/B MAC jurisdiction only; other DMEPOS items are billed to the DME MAC.

section: 10 - Where to Bill DMEPOS and PEN Items and Services
rule_text: All Part B parenteral and enteral nutrition (PEN) services are billed to the DME MAC. A provider furnishing PEN under Part B must qualify for and receive a supplier number and bill as a supplier; PEN furnished to hospital or SNF inpatients may be included in the Part A PPS rate and is not separately billable under Part B.

section: 10.1.1 - Durable Medical Equipment (DME)
rule_text: DME must meet all four definition requirements: it can withstand repeated use, is primarily and customarily used for a medical purpose, is generally not useful to a person without illness or injury, and is appropriate for use in the home.

section: 10.1.1 - Durable Medical Equipment (DME)
rule_text: A SNF normally is not considered the beneficiary's home, but it may be considered the home for Method II home dialysis purposes under applicable guidelines.

section: 10.1.2 - Prosthetic Devices - Coverage Definition
rule_text: A non-dental prosthetic device replaces all or part of an internal body organ or its function when the organ is permanently inoperative or malfunctioning. Repairs and replacements are covered when furnished incident to physician services or on a physician's order.

section: 10.1.3 - Prosthetics and Orthotics - Coverage Definition
rule_text: Leg, arm, back, and neck braces, trusses, and artificial limbs, arms, and eyes are covered when furnished incident to physician services or on a physician's order. A brace includes rigid or semi-rigid devices that support a weak or deformed body member or restrict or eliminate motion in a diseased or injured body part.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: Payment may be made for medically necessary DME, subject to the applicable HCPCS coverage status or, if the item is not listed, an MAC-developed coverage determination.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: Repairs are separately payable only when the DME is being purchased or is already owned by the patient and the repair is necessary to make it serviceable; Medicare pays the least expensive alternative, subject to applicable dialysis-system exceptions.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: Maintenance is separately payable only for equipment being purchased or already owned when the maintenance is extensive and amounts to repairs requiring skilled technicians. Routine maintenance or periodic servicing such as testing, cleaning, checking, or oiling is denied, subject to applicable dialysis-system exceptions.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: Delivery of rented or purchased equipment is covered, but payment is included in the item's fee schedule amount. Additional delivery payment may be allowed only in special circumstances at the MAC's discretion.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: Disposable supplies, such as oxygen, and replacement essential accessories such as hoses, tubes, and mouthpieces are separately payable only when essential to the effective use of medically necessary DME; replacement accessories generally require that the beneficiary own or be purchasing the DME.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: A supply claim must indicate that the patient has the DME for which the supply is intended, that the DME remains medically necessary, and that the supplies are readily identifiable as the type customarily used with the equipment. Excessive quantities or undue frequency may trigger additional review.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: DME must be intended for use in the patient's residence other than a health care institution. Payment is not made for equipment used in participating hospitals, emergency hospitals, qualifying hospitals, participating SNFs, or qualifying SNFs, with a limited exception for a nonparticipating portion of a facility that includes a distinct-part SNF.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: DMEPOS furnished to hospice patients is generally included in the hospice payment and is separately covered only when provided to treat a condition or illness unrelated to the terminal illness.

section: 10.2 - Coverage Table for DME Claims
rule_text: The supplier must maintain and provide to the MAC upon request the treating physician's detailed written order or, when required under the applicable prior rules, the CMN.

section: 10.3 - Beneficiaries Previously Enrolled in Managed Care Who Return to Traditional FFS
rule_text: A beneficiary returning from Medicare managed care to FFS must satisfy FFS benefit, coverage, and documentation requirements for items previously furnished by the plan. Such equipment is treated as newly obtained under FFS, including a new rental period for a capped rental item.

section: 10.3 - Beneficiaries Previously Enrolled in Managed Care Who Return to Traditional FFS
rule_text: For a beneficiary previously in FFS who received a capped rental item, then remained in an HMO for 60 or fewer days before returning to FFS, the capped-rental exception applies; CMS treats HMO enrollment of 60 or more days as an end of medical necessity.

section: 10.3 - Beneficiaries Previously Enrolled in Managed Care Who Return to Traditional FFS
rule_text: For home oxygen beginning with FFS coverage after managed care, the supplier must obtain and submit an initial CMN. The blood gas study need not be within 30 days before the CMN's initial certification date, but must be the most recent study obtained while in the HMO under DME MAC policy; HMO qualification alone does not establish FFS oxygen qualification.

section: 20 - Calculation and Update of Payment Rates
rule_text: Part B DME and prosthetic/orthotic payment is limited to the lower of the supplier's actual charge or the applicable fee schedule amount. PEN services paid on or after January 1, 2002 are also paid under a fee schedule.

section: 20.1 - Update Frequency
rule_text: The DMEPOS fee schedule is updated annually for update factors and quarterly to add new codes and correct errors.

section: 20.2 - Locality
rule_text: For services furnished on or after January 1, 1987, the United States is treated as one locality for DMEPOS payment purposes; enteral and parenteral therapies use a national medical service area concept.

section: 20.3 - Elimination of 'Kit' Codes and Pricing of Replacement Codes
rule_text: Effective January 1, 2002, dialysis supply kit codes were deleted. Suppliers must bill dialysis supplies using HCPCS codes for each individual supply item furnished.

section: 20.4 - Contents of Fee Schedule File
rule_text: The CMS fee schedule file contains covered DMEPOS HCPCS codes and related prices, including updates and national limitation changes, but does not contain fees for drugs used with DME or items lacking an established fee schedule amount.

section: 20.4 - Contents of Fee Schedule File
rule_text: DMEPOS fee schedule payment classes include inexpensive/routinely purchased DME, frequency-service DME, capped rental, oxygen and oxygen equipment, ostomy/tracheostomy/urological items, surgical dressings, prosthetics and orthotics, supplies, and TENS.

section: 20.5 - Online Pricing Files for DMEPOS
rule_text: A/B MACs (B) and DME MACs must maintain at least five full calendar years of DMEPOS fee schedules and related pricing data, consisting of the current year and four prior calendar years.

section: 20.6 - Phase-in For Competitive Bid Rates in Areas Not in a Competitive Bid Area
rule_text: For certain DME furnished in noncompetitive bid areas during 2016, payment used a blend of 50 percent of the competitive-bidding adjusted amount and 50 percent of the unadjusted fee schedule amount through December 31, 2016. Beginning January 1, 2017, payment used 100 percent of the adjusted amount; repriced Cures Act adjustments use RARC N689.

section: 30 - General Payment Rules
rule_text: DMEPOS is assigned to one of six payment classes: inexpensive or routinely purchased DME, frequent and substantial servicing items, customized items, other prosthetic and orthotic devices, capped rental items, or oxygen and oxygen equipment. CMS assigns each HCPCS code to a class.

section: 30 - General Payment Rules
rule_text: DME, including DME furnished under the home health or Part B benefit, and oxygen equipment are paid under fee schedules. Prosthetics and orthotics are fee-schedule items regardless of whether billed to an A/B MAC or DME MAC.

section: 30 - General Payment Rules
rule_text: DME or oxygen furnished to inpatients during a Part A-covered hospital or SNF stay is included in the PPS rate. If the inpatient is not entitled to Part A, Part B payment is still unavailable because a hospital or SNF is not the patient's home; separate billing may resume after discharge.

section: 30 - General Payment Rules
rule_text: Supplies necessary for effective use of DME are generally paid under the fee schedule for providers and suppliers other than HHAs, while drugs used with DME follow drug payment methodology. Surgical dressings are fee-schedule items except when applied incident to physician professional services, furnished by an HHA, or applied during treatment in an outpatient hospital department.

section: 30.1 - Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Inexpensive or routinely purchased DME may be billed as a rental or lump-sum purchase, but, except for TENS, total payment may not exceed the actual charge or the purchase fee schedule amount.

section: 30.1 - Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Inexpensive DME is equipment with a purchase price not exceeding $150.

section: 30.1 - Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Other routinely purchased DME is equipment acquired by purchase at least 75 percent of the time. The category includes specified nebulizer, aspirator, and ventilator accessories and, effective October 1, 2015, speech-generating devices and accessories necessary for their effective use.

section: 30.1.1 - Used Equipment
rule_text: For payment purposes, used equipment is treated as routinely purchased equipment and includes equipment previously purchased or rented by anyone, as well as equipment used without a commercial transaction, such as a trial or demonstrator unit.

section: 30.1.1 - Used Equipment
rule_text: When a beneficiary rents brand-new equipment and later purchases it, the purchase payment may be increased so that combined rental and purchase payments reach at least the fee schedule amount for comparable new equipment, but the purchase payment cannot exceed the actual purchase charge.

section: 30.1 - Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: MACs pay for these items as rentals or lump-sum purchases, but except for TENS, total payment may not exceed the actual charge or the purchase fee schedule amount.

section: 30.1 - Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Inexpensive DME is equipment with a purchase price of $150 or less.

section: 30.1 - Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Other routinely purchased DME is equipment acquired by purchase at least 75 percent of the time. The category includes specified nebulizer, aspirator, and ventilator accessories, and, effective October 1, 2015, speech-generating devices and accessories necessary for their effective use.

section: 30.1.1 - Used Equipment
rule_text: Used equipment is treated as routinely purchased equipment and includes equipment previously purchased or rented, as well as equipment used without a commercial transaction, such as a trial or demonstrator item.

section: 30.1.1 - Used Equipment
rule_text: When brand-new equipment is first rented and then purchased by the beneficiary, the purchase allowance may be calculated so combined rental and purchase payments reach the fee schedule amount for comparable new equipment, but the allowance cannot exceed the actual purchase charge.

section: 30.1.1.2 - Used Rental Equipment
rule_text: When a beneficiary purchases previously rented inexpensive or routinely purchased DME, and the claim includes modifier UE, the allowed amount is the lower of the used-equipment purchase fee schedule amount minus prior rental payments or the actual charge for the used equipment.

section: 30.1.2 - Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulator (TENS)
rule_text: For TENS, MACs pay 10 percent of the purchase price for each of two months to allow time to determine medical appropriateness. The purchase and maintenance-and-servicing amounts follow frequently purchased item rules, but the purchase allowance is not reduced by the two rental payments.

section: 30.1.2 - Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulator (TENS)
rule_text: For dates of service on or after June 8, 2012, TENS coverage for chronic low back pain is limited to the conditions in NCD Manual section 160.27.

section: 30.2 - Items Requiring Frequent and Substantial Servicing
rule_text: Items requiring frequent and substantial servicing are paid only on a fee-schedule rental basis while medical necessity continues; Medicare does not pay for their purchase.

section: 30.2.1 - Daily Payment for Continuous Passive Motion (CPM) Devices
rule_text: CPM device HCPCS E0935 is covered for beneficiaries who have received a total knee replacement only when use begins within two days after surgery and is limited to the portion of the three-week postoperative period during which the device is used in the beneficiary's home.

section: 30.2.1 - Daily Payment for Continuous Passive Motion (CPM) Devices
rule_text: MACs pay E0935 for each day it is used in the home. No payment is made for days it is not used at home or after 21 days; the hospital-discharge date counts as day one if the device is used at home that day.

section: 30.3 - Certain Customized Items
rule_text: A customized item must be uniquely constructed or substantially modified for a specific beneficiary according to a physician's description and orders, and must be so different from other items serving the same purpose that it cannot be grouped for pricing.

section: 30.3 - Certain Customized Items
rule_text: Items merely measured, assembled, fitted, adapted, or ordered with available customized features or components for an individual do not qualify as customized items unless they are uniquely constructed from raw materials or require a necessary, substantial modification to the base equipment.

section: 30.3 - Certain Customized Items
rule_text: Customized options, accessories, or custom fitting of parts alone do not make a wheelchair or other equipment a customized item for payment purposes.

section: 30.3 - Certain Customized Items
rule_text: Payment for a qualifying customized item is a lump-sum purchase based on the MAC's individual determination of a reasonable amount. The MAC considers documented reasonable labor, design, fabrication, assembly, and material costs and may require a detailed construction and labor description.

section: 30.4 - Other Prosthetic and Orthotic Devices
rule_text: Other prosthetic and orthotic devices exclude items requiring frequent and substantial servicing, customized items, parenteral or enteral nutrition supplies and equipment, and intraocular lenses. All other items in this category are paid on a lump-sum purchase basis at the fee schedule amount.

section: 30.5 - Capped Rental Items
rule_text: Capped rental DME is paid at the fee schedule amount on a monthly rental basis for no more than 15 months of continuous use. The beneficiary receives a purchase option in the tenth rental month; electric wheelchairs also require a purchase option when first furnished.

section: 30.5 - Capped Rental Items
rule_text: If the tenth-month purchase option is accepted, rental payments continue through 13 continuous rental months and title then passes to the beneficiary. If it is declined or not exercised, rental continues through the 15-month cap and title remains with the supplier.

section: 30.5.1 - Capped Rental Fee Variation by Month of Rental
rule_text: Capped-rental fees are limited to 10 percent of the applicable average allowed purchase price for each of the first three rental months and 7.5 percent for each remaining month. After 15 months, no further payment is made except the six-month maintenance-and-servicing fee.

section: 30.5.2 - Purchase Option for Capped Rental Items
rule_text: Suppliers must offer the beneficiary the option to convert capped rental equipment to a purchase during the tenth continuous rental month. Rental payments after the eleventh month are suspended until the supplier notifies the MAC that the offer was made.

section: 30.5.2 - Purchase Option for Capped Rental Items
rule_text: The beneficiary has one month from the supplier's offer to accept the purchase option. If accepted, Medicare pays through the 13th continuous rental month only, and the supplier must transfer title on the day after the 13th month is paid.

section: 30.5.3 - Additional Purchase Option for Electric Wheelchairs
rule_text: For an electric wheelchair, the supplier must offer purchase when the item is first furnished. The MAC makes no first-month rental payment until the supplier reports that the option was provided; an initial election to purchase is paid as a lump-sum fee-schedule purchase.

section: 30.5.3 - Additional Purchase Option for Electric Wheelchairs
rule_text: If the beneficiary initially declines to purchase an electric wheelchair, it is paid under capped-rental rules, including the tenth-month purchase option.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: When use ends or the beneficiary dies during a rental month, the full month rental is payable. After 15 rental months, the supplier must provide the equipment without additional charge, except for maintenance and servicing, until medical necessity ends or Medicare coverage ceases.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: Medical necessity is presumed to continue unless there is a break in need of at least 60 days. A temporary interruption may last up to 60 consecutive days plus the days remaining in the 30-day rental period; unpaid interruption months do not count toward the 15-month cap.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: If an interruption extends beyond the permitted period, no additional rental is paid until use resumes, and the MAC establishes a new date of service when use resumes.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: A new 15-month rental period after an interruption longer than 60 days plus the remaining rental-month days requires a new prescription, new medical-necessity documentation, and a supplier statement showing that medical necessity ended in the prior episode. Without this documentation, no new rental period begins.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: A change of beneficiary address, whether temporary or permanent, does not create a new rental episode.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: Changing to different but similar equipment does not create a new rental period unless medical review determines that the beneficiary's needs substantially changed and the new equipment is necessary. Otherwise, rental months continue under the existing cap and payment is based on the least expensive medically appropriate configuration.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: If medically necessary features are added to existing equipment, the original equipment continues under its existing 15-month period and the added equipment begins a separate 15-month rental period.

section: 30.5.4 - Payments for Capped Rental Items During a Period of Continuous Use
rule_text: A change in supplier does not create a new rental episode. The replacement supplier receives only the remaining rental months, and the supplier paid for the 15th month is responsible for furnishing the equipment and subsequent maintenance and servicing.

section: 30.5.5 - Payment for Power-Operated Vehicles that May Be Appropriately Used as Wheelchair
rule_text: The allowed amount for a power-operated vehicle usable as a wheelchair, including medically necessary accessories, is the lower of the actual charge or the vehicle's fee schedule amount.

section: 30.6 - Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: Oxygen and oxygen equipment are paid as a monthly fee-schedule amount per beneficiary covering equipment, contents, and supplies unless otherwise specified; purchases are not paid.

section: 30.6 - Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: Part B does not pay for DME or oxygen provided in a hospital or SNF to an inpatient not entitled to Part A. The oxygen fee schedule also does not apply to outpatients using equipment or receiving oxygen in a hospital or SNF when they do not take the equipment or system home.

section: 30.6 - Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: For oxygen claims with dates of service on or after September 27, 2021, coverage must satisfy NCD Manual section 240.2. Coverage for cluster-headache oxygen for dates through September 26, 2021 follows NCD section 240.2.2; for later dates, MACs make determinations under the applicable home-oxygen coverage rules.

section: 30.6.1 - Adjustments to Monthly Oxygen Fee
rule_text: The stationary oxygen rental fee is reduced by 50 percent when prescribed flow is less than 1 liter per minute and increased by 50 percent when stationary prescribed flow exceeds 4 liters per minute.

section: 30.6.1 - Adjustments to Monthly Oxygen Fee
rule_text: If both a volume adjustment and portable add-on could apply, MACs use only the higher applicable add-on and may not pay both. The stationary/rest flow is used when rates differ by system or activity, and the average of day and night rates is used when those rates differ.

section: 30.6.1 - Adjustments to Monthly Oxygen Fee
rule_text: When portable oxygen is prescribed, the portable equipment fee is added to the stationary oxygen rental fee.

section: 30.6.3 - Contents Only Fee
rule_text: When the beneficiary owns stationary liquid or gaseous oxygen equipment, Medicare pays the monthly oxygen contents fee, but no contents fee is paid for an owned oxygen concentrator. A portable contents fee may be paid when the beneficiary owns a concentrator or lacks owned or rented stationary gaseous or liquid equipment and has a portable system.

section: 30.6.4 - DMEPOS Clinical Trials and Demonstrations
rule_text: Modifier QR means the item or service was provided in a Medicare-specified study. DME MACs recognize QR for CMS-identified oxygen home-therapy clinical trials and pay when arterial oxygen partial pressure is 56-65 mmHg or oxygen saturation is at least 89 percent.

section: 30.6.4 - DMEPOS Clinical Trials and Demonstrations
rule_text: Condition code 30 means qualified clinical trial. For the specified oxygen home-therapy trial, A/B MACs (HHH) recognize condition code 30 with the applicable V70.7 or Z00.6 diagnosis in the second diagnosis position and pay under the same oxygen measurement thresholds.

section: 30.7 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (PEN) Items and Services
rule_text: PEN nutrients and supplies are paid as lump-sum purchases, while PEN equipment is paid monthly when rented.

section: 30.7.1 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: Parenteral and enteral pump rentals are limited to 15 total months during a period of medical need and generally follow capped-rental rules. Medical need ends when the applicable nutrients are not medically necessary for two consecutive months.

section: 30.7.1 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: No additional pump rental is allowed after 15 months or after pump purchase unless the attending physician changes the prescription between parenteral and enteral nutrients.

section: 30.7.1 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: A supplier change does not restart the 15-month period; the new supplier receives only the remaining months. The supplier paid for the 15th month must ensure pump availability through the duration of medical necessity and provide maintenance and servicing.

section: 30.7.1 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: Voluntary nonbilling care and institutional care do not count toward the 15-month limit, and an entire month's rent may not be paid when the patient is hospitalized during that month.

section: 30.7.1 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: Before approving another 15-month rental period, the DME MAC requests documentation verifying a break in medical need of at least two months.

section: 30.7.1 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: The beneficiary may purchase or rent the pump. The MAC must obtain written authorization for a purchase, and if purchase follows rental, the purchase allowance is the used-purchase allowance less rental amounts previously allowed.

section: 30.7.1 - Payment for Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: Coverage is limited to one pump for parenteral nutrition; portable or additional pumps are not separately covered.

section: 30.7.2 - Payment for PEN Supply Kits
rule_text: Enteral care kits include supplies necessary for syringe, gravity, or pump administration, and parenteral care kits and components are all-inclusive for the monthly therapy period.

section: 30.7.2 - Payment for PEN Supply Kits
rule_text: The DME MAC compares the billed enteral kit with the administration method documented on the CMN. If a pump kit is billed without acceptable pump documentation, payment is limited to the gravity-fed kit allowance, and components included in the kit are not paid separately.

section: 30.8 - Payment for Home Dialysis Supplies and Equipment
rule_text: For dates of service before January 1, 2011, home dialysis was paid under Method I through the dialysis facility or Method II through a DME supplier for supplies and services other than physician services; Method I used the composite rate and Method II physician services used monthly capitation.

section: 30.8.1 - DME MAC and A/B MAC (A) Determination of ESRD Method Selection
rule_text: For pre-2011 services, a beneficiary selected Method I or II using Form CMS-382, and Method II claims were denied when no method selection or a Method I selection was recorded at CWF.

section: 30.8.3 - Elimination of Method II Home Dialysis
rule_text: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2011, Method II is no longer a beneficiary option; all home dialysis claims must be billed by an ESRD facility and paid under the ESRD PPS, and CMS-382 submission is no longer required. Pre-2011 Method II claims may continue to process under timely-filing rules.

section: 30.8.3 - Elimination of Method II Home Dialysis
rule_text: Certain ESRD supply HCPCS codes may be separately billed for services unrelated to ESRD dialysis treatment when submitted by suppliers on a CMS-1500 or electronic equivalent with modifier AY, subject to ESRD consolidated-billing requirements.

section: 30.8.3 - Elimination of Method II Home Dialysis
rule_text: DME suppliers cannot bill or receive payment for equipment and supplies listed as never separately payable to DME suppliers because they are used only for ESRD treatment, including when modifier AY is used.

section: 30.8.2 - Installation and Delivery Charges for ESRD Equipment
rule_text: ESRD facilities are responsible for reasonable and necessary initial installation expenses, except home-improvement costs beyond what is needed to connect with existing power or water lines. Delivery and installation involving equipment testing and performance assurance may be payable when customary and commonly charged by suppliers.

section: 30.9 - Payment of DMEPOS Items Based on Modifiers
rule_text: Modifiers AU, AV, and AW identify items furnished with urological/ostomy/tracheostomy supplies, prosthetic or orthotic devices, and surgical dressings, respectively.

section: 30.9 - Payment of DMEPOS Items Based on Modifiers
rule_text: For items A4450 and A4452 furnished on or after January 1, 2005, providers must report all applicable AU, AV, and AW modifiers. For A4217 furnished with a urological, ostomy, or tracheostomy supply on or after that date, AU is required; A4217 furnished with DME is reported without a modifier, and payment depends on modifier presence or absence.

section: 30.9 - Payment of DMEPOS Items Based on Modifiers
rule_text: For replacement facial prostheses L8040-L8047 furnished on or after January 1, 2005, providers must report KM when a new impression or moulage is used and KN when the previous master model is used. KM and KN are used only for replacements, and payment is based on the reported modifier.

section: 30.9 - Payment of DMEPOS Items Based on Modifiers
rule_text: Modifier KF identifies DME classified by the FDA as a class III device. For claims with dates of service on or after January 1, 2005, HHAs must submit KF with the applicable HCPCS code for all such DME.

section: 30.9 - Payment of DMEPOS Items Based on Modifiers
rule_text: For elevating or stair-climbing power wheelchairs, the base is billed as K0011-KF, the elevation feature as E2300, and the stair-climbing feature as A9270 for the specified post-2003 claims. Older HHA claims use E1399 before January 1, 2005 and K0011-KF on or after that date.

section: 30.9 - Payment of DMEPOS Items Based on Modifiers
rule_text: Modifier KU identifies specified DMEPOS items subject to the competitive-bidding program and was required for wheelchair accessories and seat or back cushions furnished with Group 3 complex rehabilitative power wheelchairs K0848-K0864 during the applicable 2016-2017 claim periods. Beginning July 1, 2017, KU-billed items in this context are paid using unadjusted fee schedule amounts.

section: 30.9.1 - Processing of Expatriate Beneficiary DMEPOS Claims for Purchased Items Submitted with the EX Modifier
rule_text: DMEPOS furnished to a beneficiary living outside the United States is payable only when delivery occurs while the beneficiary is in the United States and the item is delivered to a U.S. address. For purchased-only items furnished on or after July 1, 2016, suppliers use modifier EX and bill based on supplier locality.

section: 30.9.1 - Processing of Expatriate Beneficiary DMEPOS Claims for Purchased Items Submitted with the EX Modifier
rule_text: Modifier EX attests that the beneficiary is an expatriate, was present in the United States when the item was delivered or furnished, and all other billing requirements were met. Suppliers must append EX to every line with a line-item date of service; claims with any line missing EX are automatically denied.

section: 30.9.1 - Processing of Expatriate Beneficiary DMEPOS Claims for Purchased Items Submitted with the EX Modifier
rule_text: A beneficiary-submitted 1490S claim requires written supplier attestation and is denied unless a supplier claim with EX or an attestation confirms the beneficiary was in the United States when furnished.

section: 30.9.1 - Processing of Expatriate Beneficiary DMEPOS Claims for Purchased Items Submitted with the EX Modifier
rule_text: Expatriate claims for oxygen equipment or supplies, PEN equipment or supplies, and capped-rental or inexpensive/routinely purchased rentals are not payable.

section: 30.9.1 - Processing of Expatriate Beneficiary DMEPOS Claims for Purchased Items Submitted with the EX Modifier
rule_text: National Mail Order and National Competitive Bid Program rules apply to expatriate claims. Mail-order supply deliveries may not use post-office boxes or lock boxes and must be delivered to the beneficiary's residence; paper claims are permitted as an exception for competitive-bid expatriate claims and must be sent to the supplier's jurisdiction.

section: unlabeled (KU modifier)
rule_text: Payment for items furnished in connection with a Group 3 complex rehabilitative power wheelchair and billed with modifier KU is based on the unadjusted fee schedule amounts, updated under section 1834(a)(14) of the Social Security Act.

section: 30.9.1 – Processing of Expatriate Beneficiary DMEPOS Claims for Purchased Items Submitted with the EX Modifier
rule_text: DMEPOS provided to a Medicare beneficiary living outside the United States is payable only when delivery occurs while the beneficiary is in the United States and the item is delivered to a U.S. address.

section: 30.9.1 – EX modifier
rule_text: For purchased-only DMEPOS items furnished on or after July 1, 2016, suppliers may use modifier EX for expatriate beneficiaries. The supplier must submit the claim based on its own locality, and use of EX attests that the beneficiary is an expatriate, was present in the United States when the item was delivered or furnished, and all other billing criteria were met.

section: 30.9.1 – EX modifier
rule_text: The EX modifier must be appended to every claim line that has a line-item date of service. A claim is automatically denied when any line item lacks EX.

section: 30.9.1 – Beneficiary-submitted claims
rule_text: A beneficiary-submitted Form 1490S claim involving an expatriate DMEPOS item must include written supplier attestation and must be supported by a supplier Form 1500 claim with EX or written attestation that the beneficiary was in the United States when the service was rendered; otherwise the 1490S claim is denied, whether or not EX is present.

section: 30.9.1 – Nonpayable expatriate items
rule_text: Expatriate claims for oxygen equipment and supplies, parenteral and enteral nutrition equipment and supplies, and rental items—including capped rental and inexpensive or routinely purchased rental items—are not payable.

section: 30.9.1 – Expatriate claims
rule_text: National Mail Order rules and National Competitive Bid Program rules apply to expatriate claims. Paper claims are permitted as an exception for CBP claims, but must be sent to the supplier’s jurisdiction for processing.

section: 30.9.1 – Expatriate delivery
rule_text: P.O. boxes and lock boxes may not be used for National Mail Order or expatriate supply deliveries; supplies must be delivered to the beneficiary’s residence.

section: 30.9.1 – Supplier attestation
rule_text: An inaccurate expatriate attestation may subject the supplier to sanctions for providing inaccurate claim information.

section: 40.1 – General maintenance and service
rule_text: Payment may be made for reasonable and necessary maintenance and servicing of purchased equipment in the inexpensive or frequently purchased, customized, other prosthetic and orthotic, and qualifying capped rental classes.

section: 40.1 – General maintenance and service
rule_text: Maintenance and servicing are not payable for purchased equipment requiring frequent and substantial servicing or for purchased oxygen equipment, except for such items purchased before June 1, 1989.

section: 40.1 – General maintenance and service
rule_text: Covered maintenance and servicing charges include only parts and labor not covered by a manufacturer or supplier warranty. Payment is made as a lump sum on an as-needed basis after individual consideration of the item.

section: 40.1 – General maintenance and service
rule_text: Maintenance and servicing of rented equipment is not payable except for PEN pumps under section 40.3, the capped-rental maintenance fee under section 40.2, and the specified oxygen-equipment maintenance fee under 42 CFR 414.210(e)(2).

section: 40.1 – General maintenance and service
rule_text: Servicing equipment that the beneficiary is purchasing or already owns is covered when necessary to make it serviceable and may include required loaner equipment. Payment is limited to the lesser of the servicing expense or the estimated cost of purchasing or renting another item for the remaining period of medical need.

section: 40.1 – General maintenance and service
rule_text: Claims suggesting malicious damage, culpable neglect, or wrongful disposition of equipment must be investigated and denied when program payment would be unreasonable, with referral to the regional office program-integrity specialist.

section: 40.2 – Maintenance and Service of Capped Rental Items
rule_text: For capped rental items furnished before January 1, 2006 that reached the 13-month rental cap, maintenance and servicing fees are payable only after six months have elapsed from the end of the final paid rental month or from the end of warranty coverage, whichever is later.

section: 40.2 – Maintenance and Service of Capped Rental Items
rule_text: For pre-2006 capped rental items, the maintenance and servicing fee may be paid no more than once every six months. If the beneficiary elected purchase, maintenance and servicing follow the purchased-equipment rules in section 40.1.

section: 40.2 – Maintenance and Service of Capped Rental Items
rule_text: For capped rental items furnished on or after January 1, 2006, reasonable and necessary maintenance and servicing is payable for beneficiary-owned equipment after 13 months of continuous use. This also applies to complex rehabilitative power wheelchairs acquired by lump-sum purchase and to capped rental items titled to the beneficiary before 13 months after one or more rental payments.

section: 40.3 – Maintenance and Service of PEN Pumps
rule_text: After the 15-month rental limit, necessary PEN pump maintenance may include repairs or extensive maintenance involving sealed components or specialized testing. The DME MAC pays only for actual maintenance, servicing, or replacement incidents and requires written supplier proof.

section: 40.3 – Maintenance and Service of PEN Pumps
rule_text: For enteral pumps, payment is limited to one-half of a rental payment every six months beginning six months after the last rental payment. For parenteral pumps, payment is limited to one-half of a rental payment every three months beginning three months after the last rental payment.

section: 50 – Payment for Replacement of Equipment
rule_text: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2023, providers and suppliers no longer submit CMNs or DIFs with claims; claims received with attached forms are rejected and returned. For earlier dates of service, required CMNs or DIFs must still be submitted or already on file.

section: 50 – Payment for Replacement of Equipment
rule_text: Replacement of beneficiary-owned, beneficiary-purchased, or capped-rental equipment is covered for loss, irreparable damage, wear, or a change in the patient’s condition, subject to the applicable documentation and medical-necessity requirements.

section: 50 – Payment for Replacement of Equipment
rule_text: Replacement for loss or irreparable damage may be reimbursed without a physician order when the DME MAC determines that the original order, considering its age, still meets the patient’s medical needs. Replacement due to wear or a change in condition requires a current physician order.

section: 50 – Payment for Replacement of Equipment
rule_text: Replacement of rented equipment is not payable except for capped rental items. Purchased replacement may be paid for inexpensive or routinely purchased items, customized items, capped rental items purchased by the beneficiary, and other prosthetic and orthotic devices.

section: 50 – Payment for Replacement of Equipment
rule_text: Purchase or replacement is not payable for items requiring frequent and substantial servicing or for oxygen equipment, subject to the separate oxygen replacement provisions.

section: 50 – Payment for Replacement of Equipment
rule_text: Cases suggesting malicious damage, culpable neglect, or wrongful disposition must be investigated and denied when payment would be unreasonable, with referral to the regional office program-integrity specialist.

section: 50.1 – Payment for Replacement of Capped Rental Items
rule_text: A new capped-rental item may be obtained when the existing item has been in continuous use, on a rental or purchase basis, for its useful lifetime, or when it is lost or irreparably damaged. The MAC determines useful lifetime, which cannot be less than five years, and measures it from delivery to the beneficiary rather than the equipment’s manufacture or acquisition date.

section: 50.1 – Payment for Replacement of Capped Rental Items
rule_text: When a beneficiary elects a replacement capped-rental item, Medicare payment may be made on either a rental or purchase basis.

section: 50.3 – Payment for Replacement of Parenteral and Enteral Pumps
rule_text: Replacement of a PEN pump purchased more than eight years before the current date may be considered when documentation proves the purchase date. Medicare may pay either for replacement by purchase or for 15 months of rental.

section: 50.4 – Payment for Replacement of Oxygen Equipment in Bankruptcy Situations
rule_text: When a supplier files Chapter 7 or Chapter 11 bankruptcy and cannot continue furnishing oxygen, the oxygen equipment is treated as lost and replacement may be paid. A new useful-lifetime period and new 36-month rental period begin on delivery of the replacement equipment.

section: 50.4 – Payment for Replacement of Oxygen Equipment in Bankruptcy Situations
rule_text: Before paying replacement oxygen equipment after bankruptcy, the MAC must verify supporting court and bankruptcy documentation. Chapter 7 requires court records showing the petition; Chapter 11 requires court records showing the petition plus documentation that the equipment was or will be sold, or a court order authorizing abandonment.

section: 50.4 – Payment for Replacement of Oxygen Equipment in Bankruptcy Situations
rule_text: A replacement oxygen claim must include valid blood-gas testing results, an Oxygen CMN, the replacement oxygen HCPCS code, modifier RA, and a narrative explaining why the equipment was replaced.

section: 50.4 – Payment for Replacement of Oxygen Equipment in Bankruptcy Situations
rule_text: Payment is prohibited when the original supplier divests its business and equipment outside the court-supervised bankruptcy process.

section: 50.5 – Payment of a Part of a DMEPOS Item
rule_text: Modifier RB identifies replacement of a part of a DMEPOS base item furnished as part of repairing that item. All repair-part claims billed with RB are paid on a lump-sum purchase basis, whether or not the item is furnished in a competitive bidding area.

section: 50.5 – Payment of a Part of a DMEPOS Item
rule_text: For RB repair parts described by competitive-bidding HCPCS codes and used to repair competitive-bid base equipment in a competitive bidding area, payment is based on the applicable single payment amount. For parts used to repair noncompetitive base equipment, payment is determined under the applicable regulatory methodology, and the contractor may use the single payment amount when establishing the allowed amount.

section: 60 – Payment for Delivery and Service Charges for Durable Medical Equipment
rule_text: Delivery and service costs for oxygen and DME are ordinarily included in the fee schedule and may not be billed separately except as specifically authorized or in rare and unusual circumstances involving atypical delivery operations.

section: 60 – Payment for Delivery and Service Charges for Durable Medical Equipment
rule_text: A separate delivery charge may be allowed when extraordinary delivery is necessary, such as delivery to a remote area without a local supplier or when a local supplier is temporarily out of stock. If the item could have been obtained locally, any additional charge cannot raise total payment above the local fee schedule amount.

section: 60 – Payment for Delivery and Service Charges for Durable Medical Equipment
rule_text: When separately payable, delivery charges must be based on relevant circumstances including travel time and distance, actual additional expenses, type and quantity of equipment, customary and prevailing local charges, and comparable charges elsewhere. Charges may be paid only for deliveries actually made.

section: 60 – Payment for Delivery and Service Charges for Durable Medical Equipment
rule_text: Suppliers should bill separate delivery charges only for unusual circumstances and must fully document those circumstances on claims or bills. Routine itemization may result in delivery charges being treated as included in the equipment fee.

section: 80 – Penalty Charges for Late Payment
rule_text: Penalty charges imposed on a beneficiary by a physician or supplier for failure to pay a bill on time are not covered by Medicare.

section: 90 – Payment for Additional Expenses for Deluxe Features
rule_text: Payment for rented or purchased equipment must be limited to what is reasonable and medically necessary for the intended purpose. Deluxe features, aesthetic items, and convenience features are not payable above the amount for the standard item, ordinarily the least costly item, unless the additional feature is medically necessary.

section: 90 – Payment for Additional Expenses for Deluxe Features
rule_text: A supplier may not charge a beneficiary for medically unnecessary features unless the beneficiary or representative specifically requested the deluxe item with knowledge of the charge and an ABN documents the informed request.

section: 90 – Payment for Additional Expenses for Deluxe Features
rule_text: An assigned supplier must accept the allowed charge for medically necessary equipment or services as payment in full and may not bill the beneficiary for the differential attributable to a more expensive item actually furnished. A supplier wishing to collect the full price of equipment exceeding medical need must not accept assignment.

section: 90 – Payment for Additional Expenses for Deluxe Features
rule_text: In an assignment case, the beneficiary is responsible for any unpaid balance of the allowed charge when Medicare payments stop because the equipment is no longer medically necessary; the beneficiary’s estate is responsible when payments stop because of death.

section: 100 – General Documentation Requirements
rule_text: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2023, CMNs and DIFs are not submitted with claims and attached forms cause rejection and return. For dates before January 1, 2023, existing CMN/DIF submission or prior-file requirements remain unchanged.

section: 100.1 – Written Order Prior to Delivery
rule_text: Suppliers, including providers billing DME MACs or A/B MACs as suppliers, must follow the written-order-before-delivery requirements in the Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 5.

section: 100.2 – Certificates of Medical Necessity
rule_text: For certain DMEPOS items billed to a DME MAC, the supplier must obtain a signed CMN from the treating physician. HHAs billing the same items to an A/B MAC (HHH) use signed physician orders in the home-health plan of care instead, and DME MACs may request supporting documentation beyond the CMN.

section: 100.2.1 – Completion of Certificate of Medical Necessity Forms
rule_text: A CMN must identify the certification type and applicable initial, revised, or recertification dates; beneficiary, supplier, physician, and Medicare identifier information; place of service and facility information when applicable; and the HCPCS codes for items requiring certification.

section: 100.2.1 – Completion of Certificate of Medical Necessity Forms
rule_text: The treating physician must review the CMN and sign and date it, certifying the information and medical necessity of the ordered items. Signature and date stamps are not acceptable, and altered certification or recertification forms are denied; suppliers showing patterns of alteration may be audited.

section: 100.2.1 – Completion of Certificate of Medical Necessity Forms
rule_text: Section B of the CMN may not be completed by the supplier; it may be completed by a clinician or physician employee but must be reviewed by the treating physician. The person answering section B must be identified unless the treating physician completed it.

section: 100.2.1 – Completion of Certificate of Medical Necessity Forms
rule_text: The CMN must state the estimated length of need; a lifetime need is represented by 99 months. Revised and recertification CMNs must include the cumulative length of need from the initial date of need.

section: 100.2.1 – Completion of Certificate of Medical Necessity Forms
rule_text: The supplier must describe each ordered item, option, accessory, supply, and drug and report the supplier charge and applicable Medicare fee schedule allowance for each.

section: 100.2.2 – Evidence of Medical Necessity for PEN Therapy
rule_text: A completed CMN must accompany and support initial PEN claims, establish that coverage criteria are met, and show that the therapy is consistent with the physician’s prescription. PEN suppliers may not complete the medical and prescription information; it must come from the patient’s records and be completed or reviewed and signed by the treating physician.

section: 100.2.2.1 – Scheduling and Documenting Certifications and Recertifications of Medical Necessity for PEN
rule_text: The initial PEN certification must accompany the initial claim and is valid for six months. The DME MAC establishes recertification timing case by case; a prescription change after the initial certification period does not restart the certification process.

section: 100.2.2.1 – Scheduling and Documenting Certifications and Recertifications of Medical Necessity for PEN
rule_text: PEN medical necessity ends after two consecutive months without medically required PEN services; if certification is required again, the process begins after those two months. A revised certification is required for specified changes in nutrient or calorie orders, parenteral volume exceeding one liter per day, mixing method, enteral/parenteral therapy, or infusion method.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: Every PEN certification must include beneficiary and certification information and supplier identification. Medical and prescription information must be completed from patient records by the attending or ordering physician or an authorized employee and reviewed and signed by the physician.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: The PEN CMN must identify the place where services are received, patient condition and expected therapy duration, diagnoses and functional impairment, and the clinical basis for therapy. The physician is generally expected to see the patient within 30 days before certifying or recertifying; if not, the physician must explain why and document other monitoring used.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: For parenteral nutrition, the CMN must state infusion frequency, administration route, justification for premixed formulas and special formulas, and amino-acid/dextrose components. Dextrose below 10 percent, more than 12 lipid units per month, and premixed solutions require physician justification.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: Renal dialysis patients receiving parenteral therapy must meet all PEN coverage requirements, including documentation of permanent functional impairment preventing swallowing or nutrient absorption; supplemental parenteral therapy alone is generally not covered.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: For enteral nutrition, the CMN must identify the nutrient product or category, calories per day, frequency, administration method, administration route, and reason for using a pump. One hundred calories equals one billing unit.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: Category IB blenderized enteral nutrients require documentation of intolerance, severe allergic reaction, or expected permanent adverse symptoms from nutritionally equivalent semisynthetic products. Categories III through VI and higher-category formulas require additional medical justification, and adverse events must be documented when moving from Category I or II products to a higher category.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: The physician must document the reason for prescribing fewer than 750 or more than 2,000 enteral calories per day.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: Enteral pumps are covered only when the attending physician documents medical necessity, including the reason syringe or gravity administration is inadequate. The DME MAC reviews whether billed equipment is consistent with the prescription, such as an IV pole when a pump is used.

section: 100.2.2.2 – Completion of the Elements of PEN CMN
rule_text: Each PEN certification must contain the attending physician’s handwritten original signature and date, reasonably associated with active therapy dates, along with complete physician identification. It must also contain the PEN supplier’s name, address, telephone number, and PEN identification number so the DME MAC can verify authorization.

section: 100.2.2.3 – DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: PEN coverage cannot begin before the physician certification date. The CMN must state the estimated duration of therapy, and the initial estimated length of need determines the recertification schedule.

section: 100.2.2.3 – DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: The certification must support the PEN supplies billed and show a diagnosis with functional impairment preventing swallowing for enteral therapy or absorption for parenteral therapy.

section: 100.2.2.3 – DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: Assigned initial PEN claims are denied without development when diagnosis or functional impairment is missing or inappropriate, therapy duration is missing or under 90 consecutive days, supplies were not provided, supplies precede the therapy onset date, or the physician signature is stamped. Unassigned claims are developed for missing or incomplete information.

section: 100.2.2.3 – Revised Certifications/Change in Prescription
rule_text: A revised PEN certification is required for changes in nutrient or calorie orders, parenteral volume exceeding one liter per day, mixing method, enteral versus parenteral therapy, or infusion method. PEN payment levels are not adjusted unless a revised or renewed certification documents the change.

section: 100.2.2.3 - DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: Each PEN certification must include the physician's provider number and PEN identification number so the DME MAC can verify supplier authorization and develop claims.

section: 100.2.2.3 - DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: PEN coverage may not begin before the physician certification date. The CMN must state the estimated duration of therapy, which is used to verify the permanence requirement and establish the recertification schedule.

section: 100.2.2.3 - DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: The certification must support the PEN supplies billed. The diagnosis must demonstrate functional impairment preventing an enteral patient from swallowing or a parenteral patient from absorbing nutrients.

section: 100.2.2.3 - DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: Assigned initial PEN claims are denied without development when the diagnosis or functional impairment is missing or inappropriate, estimated therapy duration is under 90 consecutive days or absent, supplies were not provided, supplies preceded the therapy onset date, or the physician signature is stamped.

section: 100.2.2.3 - DME MAC Review of Initial PEN Certifications
rule_text: Unassigned PEN claims with missing or incomplete certification information are developed for the missing information.

section: 100.2.2.3 - Revised Certifications/Change in Prescription
rule_text: A revised certification is required for changes in nutrient or calorie orders, a change of more than one liter in daily parenteral-solution volume, a change between home-mix and pre-mix solutions, a change between enteral and parenteral therapy, or a change in infusion method such as gravity to pump.

section: 100.2.2.3 - Revised Certifications/Change in Prescription
rule_text: PEN payment is not adjusted for a prescription change unless a revised or renewed certification documents the change. Payment under the most current certification or recertification may not be changed without a new recertification documenting the prescription change.

section: 100.2.2.3 - Revised Certifications/Change in Prescription
rule_text: The DME MAC may modify the recertification schedule when necessary.

section: 100.2.3.1 - Scheduling and Documenting Recertifications of Medical Necessity for Oxygen
rule_text: Oxygen recertifications must include the date and results of the most recent arterial blood gas or oximetry test before the recertification date, the testing provider and test conditions, and the estimated length of oxygen need in Section B of Form CMS-484.

section: 100.2.3.1 - Scheduling and Documenting Recertifications of Medical Necessity for Oxygen
rule_text: For Group I oxygen patients, the DME MAC determines recertification requirements and scheduling.

section: 100.2.3.1 - Scheduling and Documenting Recertifications of Medical Necessity for Oxygen
rule_text: For Group II patients beginning coverage after January 1, 1991, recertification is required within 90 days after initial certification when the qualifying initial arterial blood gas is at least 55 mm Hg or oxygen saturation is at least 89 percent. The repeat blood gas study must occur between days 61 and 90, and retesting is required only when payment will be claimed for the fourth or later month.

section: 100.2.3.1 - Scheduling and Documenting Recertifications of Medical Necessity for Oxygen
rule_text: When a required oxygen recertification test is not performed within the specified period, the DME MAC does not pay the next month's claim. If a later qualifying test is obtained, the supplier must use the repeat-test date as the date of service on a subsequent claim, and payment resumes from that date if Group II criteria are met.

section: 100.2.3.1 - New Orders
rule_text: A new physician order must be obtained and retained, without a new CMN or repeat blood gas study, when the prescribed maximum flow rate changes but remains within the same category—less than 1 LPM, 1-4 LPM, or greater than 4 LPM—or when the stationary delivery system changes among concentrator, liquid, and gaseous systems.

section: 100.2.3.2 - HHA Recertification for Home Oxygen Therapy
rule_text: For patients whose initial arterial blood gas is 56 or higher or initial oxygen saturation is at least 89 percent, the HHA must arrange retesting between days 60 and 90 after oxygen begins; the three-month recertification must reflect testing performed between days 61 and 90.

section: 100.2.3.2 - HHA Recertification for Home Oxygen Therapy
rule_text: Payment for the fourth month of home oxygen requires the attending physician's certification that the qualifying retest establishes continuing medical necessity.

section: 100.2.3.2 - HHA Recertification for Home Oxygen Therapy
rule_text: HHAs must report value code 58 or 59 on every initial home-oxygen bill and on the fourth-month bill.

section: 100.2.3.2 - HHA Recertification for Home Oxygen Therapy
rule_text: For oxygen patients not under a plan of care, HHAs must obtain and retain the physician's recertification of retesting. For patients under a plan of care, HHAs must obtain the recertification and record it on Form CMS-485 or CMS-486.

section: 100.2.3.2 - HHA Recertification for Home Oxygen Therapy
rule_text: A/B MACs (HHH) must stop payment when the HHA does not have the patient retested for continuing oxygen need within the required time frames.

section: 100.2.3.3 - Review of Oxygen Certifications
rule_text: All claims with an initial certification prescribing an oxygen flow rate above 4 LPM require review before payment authorization.

section: 100.2.3.3 - Review of Oxygen Certifications
rule_text: When the treating physician specifies the oxygen equipment, the equipment furnished must be consistent with the prescription.

section: 100.2.3.3 - Review of Oxygen Certifications
rule_text: The CMN or Form CMS-484 must be signed by the treating physician; a stamped signature is unacceptable. The physician identification number must be the UPIN.

section: 100.3 - Limitations on DME MAC Collection of Information
rule_text: A CMN must accompany initial power-operated-vehicle claims. Outside audits, investigations, or individual claim development, DME MACs may not require additional documentation with every POV claim.

section: 100.3 - Limitations on DME MAC Collection of Information
rule_text: DME MACs may require the power-wheelchair make and model name or number in Section C of the CMN, but may not require it as separate documentation with every claim.

section: 100.3 - Limitations on DME MAC Collection of Information
rule_text: Suppliers are not required to submit additional documentation of a beneficiary's condition and functional abilities with every claim for equipment at a higher level than previously supplied. DME MACs may review individual claims through pre- or post-payment probes to assess medical necessity and avoid duplicate equipment.

section: 100.4 - Reporting the Ordering/Referring NPI on Claims for DMEPOS Items Dispensed Without a Physician’s Order
rule_text: For claims submitted on or after May 23, 2008, a supplier dispensing an item without a physician or other licensed-provider order must use modifier EY and report its own name and NPI in the Ordering/Referring Provider fields to obtain a Medicare denial for coordination-of-benefits purposes.

section: 100.4 - Reporting the Ordering/Referring NPI on Claims for DMEPOS Items Dispensed Without a Physician’s Order
rule_text: If an order exists for only some items provided to a beneficiary, the supplier must submit a separate claim for the items lacking an order.

section: 110 - General Billing Requirements
rule_text: Part B suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill DMEPOS to the DME MAC, except implanted DME and supplies for implanted equipment, which are billed to A/B MAC (B). Institutional providers bill prosthetic and orthotic devices and supplies to A/B MAC (A); hospital outpatient DME is billed to the appropriate DME MAC.

section: 110 - General Billing Requirements
rule_text: A supplier or provider must have an NSC-issued supplier billing number before billing the DME MAC. Beneficiary-submitted claims must contain an enrolled Medicare supplier number.

section: 110 - General Billing Requirements
rule_text: DMEPOS furnished under an HHA plan of care may be billed by the HHA or supplier to the DME MAC. If the HHA bills A/B MAC (HHH), it includes the DME on a 32X or 33X PPS claim; an HHA furnishing DMEPOS to a beneficiary not under a plan of care uses bill type 34X.

section: 110.1 - Billing/Claim Formats
rule_text: DME MAC and A/B MAC (B) claims use the ASC X12 837 professional format or, when permitted, Form CMS-1500. A/B MAC (A), including A/B MAC (HHH), claims use the ASC X12 institutional format or, when permitted, Form CMS-1450; electronic formats support CMN reporting in the FRM segment.

section: 110.1 - Billing/Claim Formats
rule_text: NCPDP Telecommunications Standard D0 and Batch Standard 1.2 are used for electronic retail-pharmacy drug claims and related coordination of benefits. Other pharmacy claims to the DME MAC must use the 837 professional format.

section: 110.1.1 - Requirements for Implementing the NCPDP Standard
rule_text: Only DME MAC suppliers with NSC specialty code A5 may use the NCPDP standard for retail pharmacy drug transactions. NDCs, rather than drug HCPCS codes, must identify prescription drugs dispensed through those transactions.

section: 110.1.2 - Certificate of Medical Necessity (CMN)
rule_text: Form CMS-852 is required for parenteral nutrition claims. Form DMERC-08.02 is not required for immunosuppressive-drug claims with dates of service on or after April 1, 2006; required CMN data must be included in the valid electronic transaction, and retail pharmacies must provide hard-copy CMNs when required on Form CMS-1500 claims.

section: 110.2 - Application of DMEPOS Fee Schedule
rule_text: The DMEPOS fee schedule applies to listed institutional bill types, including 13X, 23X, 32X, 33X, 34X, 71X, 74X, 75X, 83X, and 85X, for the orthotics/prosthetics and DME/oxygen categories shown in the manual. Unlisted bill types generally are not subject to the fee schedule, except provider-based FQHCs.

section: 110.2 - Application of DMEPOS Fee Schedule
rule_text: Hospital inpatient Part B bill type 12X and SNF inpatient Part B bill type 22X are subject to the fee schedule for orthotics/prosthetics, but DME/oxygen is not covered and therefore is not subject to the fee schedule. HHAs bill DME/oxygen to A/B MAC (HHH), while other providers bill the DME MAC.

section: 110.2 - Application of DMEPOS Fee Schedule
rule_text: For HHA bill types 32X and 33X, specified catheter and ostomy HCPCS codes are excluded from the fee schedule and catheter/ostomy supplies are treated as non-routine supplies billed with revenue code 027X. Specified hospital ASC supply codes are also excluded or conditionally included as described by the applicable code and procedure.

section: 110.2 - Application of DMEPOS Fee Schedule
rule_text: DME billing is not required on Home Health PPS claims. HHAs may bill A/B MAC (HHH) or arrange for a supplier to furnish the service and bill the DME MAC.

section: 110.3.1 - Conditions That Must Be Met
rule_text: A supplier may pre-discharge deliver DME, prosthetics, or orthotics, but not supplies, to an inpatient facility for fitting or training only when the item is medically necessary for home use and on discharge, supported by a physician order with an initial need date no later than discharge, intended for home use, delivered no earlier than two days before discharge, and taken or delivered to the beneficiary's home on discharge.

section: 110.3.1 - Conditions That Must Be Met
rule_text: Pre-discharge delivery may not shift the facility's obligation to furnish items needed during the stay; such items are included in DRG/PPS rates. The supplier may not bill for any day before discharge, may not bill extra delivery costs or redelivery to the beneficiary, and the discharge must be to a qualified home-like place of service rather than another inpatient or SNF facility that is not the beneficiary's home.

section: 110.3.2 - Date of Service for Pre-Discharge Delivery of DMEPOS
rule_text: The general DMEPOS date of service is the delivery date. For qualifying pre-discharge delivery intended for home use, the date of service is generally the discharge date, and no party may bill for days before discharge.

section: 110.3.2 - Date of Service for Pre-Discharge Delivery of DMEPOS
rule_text: If the beneficiary or caregiver takes the item home after it is left at the facility, the discharge date is the deemed delivery and claim date of service. If the supplier removes the item after fitting or training and later delivers it home, the date of service is the actual home-delivery date, which cannot precede discharge.

section: 110.3.2 - Date of Service for Pre-Discharge Delivery of DMEPOS
rule_text: If the item is left at the facility and is not taken or delivered home by discharge, the date of service cannot precede the actual date the item arrives at the beneficiary's home.

section: 110.3.3 - Facility Responsibilities During the Transition Period
rule_text: A facility remains responsible for medically necessary items throughout the beneficiary's stay, and DRG/PPS rates cover those items. The facility may not delay or prematurely remove an item or shift its cost to Medicare Part B because a supplier delivered a similar or identical item for fitting or training.

section: 110.3.3 - Facility Responsibilities During the Transition Period
rule_text: Beginning two days before discharge, the facility may reasonably allow a supplier to fit or train the beneficiary using the home-use item, including substituting it for the facility's item during the final two inpatient days when reasonable and necessary. The restrictions apply to P&O during covered Part A stays and to DME during covered Part A or Part B stays.

section: 110.4 - Frequency of Claims for Repetitive Services
rule_text: HHAs include DMEPOS on 32X or 33X claims at the frequency required for home-health visits. Other providers and suppliers, including HHAs billing 34X, generally submit repetitive-service claims monthly unless another policy permits a different frequency; suppliers may, for example, bill more than one month's diabetic test strips.

section: 110.4 - Frequency of Claims for Repetitive Services
rule_text: Claims for known continuous services, including capped rentals or therapies, must be submitted sequentially. After a break in service, such as an interruption caused by an extended inpatient stay, sequential billing continues when service resumes.

section: 110.5 - DME MACs Only - Appeals of Duplicate Claims
rule_text: For claims denied as duplicates, appeal rights are limited to whether the claim is actually a duplicate; coverage, medical necessity, pricing, and other issues may not be appealed under that denial. If the supplier establishes that the claim is not a duplicate, the DME MAC adjudicates it under all other Medicare rules.

section: 120 - DME MACs - Billing Procedures Related To ABN Upgrades
rule_text: An ABN informs the beneficiary before receipt that Medicare probably will not pay for the particular item or occasion. A supplier may collect more than Medicare's allowed amount for medically unnecessary features or upgrades only when the beneficiary liability requirements are met; a signed ABN is necessary for unassigned claims, while assigned claims require a signed ABN or other acceptable evidence of beneficiary knowledge.

section: 120 - DME MACs - Billing Procedures Related To ABN Upgrades
rule_text: An upgrade is an item with features beyond what is medically necessary, including an excess component that is additional, more extensive, or more expensive than the reasonable-and-necessary item. The upgraded item must remain medically appropriate and serve the intended medical purpose of the physician-ordered item.

section: 120 - General Instructions for ABN Upgrades
rule_text: An upgrade may be within one HCPCS code or from one HCPCS code to another; within-code upgrades must contain features exceeding the official code descriptor. An ABN may not be used to substitute an item that is medically inappropriate, and it does not change applicable coverage, payment, statutory, or billing rules.

section: 120 - General Instructions for ABN Upgrades
rule_text: If Medicare would pay for the physician-ordered item on a rental basis, the supplier must furnish the upgrade on a rental basis.

section: 120 - General Instructions for ABN Upgrades
rule_text: For an upgrade where the supplier expects a medical-necessity partial denial, the supplier must obtain a signed ABN to hold the beneficiary liable for the additional expense. The supplier must identify the upgrade features on the claim and use modifier GA on the upgraded line when a valid signed ABN is on file.

section: 120 - Billing Instructions for ABN Upgrades
rule_text: An upgraded item must be billed with two sequential lines on the same claim. Line 1 reports the HCPCS and full charge for the upgraded item, using GA when a valid ABN is signed or GZ when no valid ABN was obtained; Line 2 reports the reasonable-and-necessary HCPCS and full charge with modifier GK.

section: 120 - Billing Instructions for ABN Upgrades
rule_text: When an upgrade is within one HCPCS code, both claim lines use that same code, with the higher charge on Line 1. The two lines must be adjacent and in sequential order; assigned claims with invalid ABN upgrade information are returned or rejected, while unassigned claims are denied.

section: 120 - Definitions of Modifiers Associated With ABNs
rule_text: Modifier GA indicates waiver of liability with an ABN on file for an item expected to be denied as not reasonable and necessary; GZ indicates an item expected to be denied as not reasonable and necessary without an ABN; GK identifies the associated reasonable-and-necessary item or service.

section: 120.1 - Providing Upgrades of DMEPOS Without Any Extra Charge
rule_text: A supplier may furnish an upgraded item at no additional charge to Medicare or the beneficiary. Medicare payment and beneficiary coinsurance remain based on the allowed amount for the medically necessary non-upgraded item.

section: 120.1 - Billing Instructions
rule_text: When an upgrade is furnished at no extra charge, the supplier must bill only the non-upgraded item's HCPCS code and charge, using modifier GL. The claim must identify the make and model actually furnished and explain why it is an upgrade; any applicable CMN is completed for the non-upgraded code, not the upgraded item.

section: 130.1 - Provider Billing for Prosthetic and Orthotic Devices
rule_text: Prosthetic and orthotic devices provided during inpatient care are generally included in the Part A PPS rate unless specifically outside the rate. The DME MAC does not separately pay DME provided to a beneficiary in an SNF.

section: 130.1 - Provider Billing for Prosthetic and Orthotic Devices
rule_text: P&O devices and supplies outside the PPS rate may be billed by a supplier for an SNF or hospital to A/B MAC (A), or by a qualified outside entity to its normal contractor. Facilities furnishing P&O to patients for whom Part A benefits are not payable may bill for the items if other requirements are met.

section: 130.1 - Provider Billing for Prosthetic and Orthotic Devices
rule_text: When HHAs bill catheter and ostomy items for patients under a plan of care, the items are supplies billed under revenue code 0270. Hospitals billing specified items with an ASC service use revenue code 0272; in other listed circumstances, including HHAs without a plan of care, SNFs, CORFs, OPTs, and hospitals, the items are billed as P&O under revenue code 0274 with the relevant HCPCS code.

section: 130.1 - Provider Billing for Prosthetic and Orthotic Devices
rule_text: In states requiring licensure or certification for prosthetics or orthotics, DME MACs process prosthetics and certain custom-fabricated orthotics only for suppliers with qualifying NSC specialty codes, including 51-57, 65, 67, B5, and applicable physician specialties. The entity must be licensed or certified when required and authorized by state law; claims from other specialty codes are denied.

section: 130.2 - Billing for Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Inexpensive or routinely purchased DME includes equipment costing no more than $150, equipment purchased at least 75 percent of the time as determined by the Secretary, qualifying nebulizer/aspirator/ventilator accessories, and, effective October 1, 2015, speech-generating devices and necessary accessories.

section: 130.2 - Billing for Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Suppliers and non-HHA providers bill this category to the DME MAC, except implanted DME billed to A/B MAC (B). HHAs bill A/B MAC (HHH) or the DME MAC.

section: unlabeled
rule_text: When hospitals bill HCPCS codes A4214, A4310-A4330, A4338-A4359, or A5102-A5114 with an ASC service, the items are excluded from the DME fee schedule and must be billed as supplies under revenue code 0272.

section: unlabeled
rule_text: HCPCS codes A5119-A5131 are excluded from the fee schedule unless submitted with specified ostomy-related ASC procedure codes 44340-44346, 44380, 44382, 44388-44392, or 50953-50961.

section: unlabeled
rule_text: Except for the hospital-with-ASC circumstances described above, HHAs billing patients not under a plan of care, SNFs, CORFs, OPTs, and hospitals bill the applicable items as prosthetics and orthotics under revenue code 0274 with the relevant HCPCS code.

section: unlabeled
