rule_text: In states requiring licensure or certification to furnish prosthetics or orthotics, DME MACs process claims for prosthetics and certain custom-fabricated orthotics only when the supplier's NSC-forwarded specialty code is an authorized code, including codes 51-53, 55-57, 65, 67, B5, or an applicable physician specialty code listed in Chapter 26, section 10.8.2.

section: unlabeled
rule_text: Authorized prosthetic and orthotic specialties must be licensed or certified when required by state law and may bill Medicare only when state law permits that entity to furnish the prosthetic or orthotic. Claims from other specialty codes must be denied.

section: 130.2 - Billing for Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Inexpensive or routinely purchased DME includes equipment priced at $150 or less, equipment acquired by purchase at least 75 percent of the time, specified accessories used with nebulizers, aspirators, or qualifying ventilators, and, effective October 1, 2015, speech-generating devices and accessories necessary for their effective use.

section: 130.2 - Billing for Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill inexpensive or routinely purchased DME to the DME MAC; implanted DME is billed to the A/B MAC (B). HHAs bill the A/B MAC (HHH) or, as applicable, the DME MAC.

section: 130.2 - Billing for Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: Medicare DME coverage for seat lifts is limited to the seat-lift mechanism for items furnished on or after January 1, 1991. Chairs coded E0620 are not payable; the appropriate mechanism codes are E0627, E0628, and E0629, although an integral seat may be included in the mechanism.

section: 130.2 - Billing for Inexpensive or Other Routinely Purchased DME
rule_text: For TENS, suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill the DME MAC. HHAs bill the A/B MAC (HHH), using revenue code 0291 for the two-month rental period with each month on a separate line, and revenue code 0292 for the purchase with the appropriate HCPCS code.

section: 130.3 - Billing for Items Requiring Frequent and Substantial Servicing
rule_text: Items requiring frequent and substantial servicing include items such as intermittent positive pressure breathing machines and ventilators, but exclude ventilators that are continuous airway pressure devices or intermittent assist devices with continuous airway pressure devices.

section: 130.3 - Billing for Items Requiring Frequent and Substantial Servicing
rule_text: Suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill these items to the DME MAC; HHAs bill the A/B MAC (HHH).

section: 130.4 - Billing for Certain Customized Items
rule_text: Customized DME without a specific HCPCS code must be billed as E1399 (miscellaneous DME). This also applies when a coded item has been modified so extensively that neither its original description nor another HCPCS description accurately describes it.

section: 130.4 - Billing for Certain Customized Items
rule_text: Suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill customized items to the A/B MAC (B) or DME MAC. HHAs bill the A/B MAC (HHH) using revenue code 0292 with the HCPCS code.

section: 130.5 - Billing for Capped Rental Items (Other Items of DME)
rule_text: Capped rental items are DME other than oxygen and oxygen equipment that do not fall within the inexpensive or routinely purchased, frequently serviced, or customized-item categories.

section: 130.5 - Billing for Capped Rental Items (Other Items of DME)
rule_text: Suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill capped rental items to the DME MAC; HHAs bill the A/B MAC (HHH).

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: Stationary oxygen rental fee-schedule payments are all-inclusive monthly allowances covering stationary equipment and contents furnished during the rental month. Suppliers must bill stationary oxygen equipment and contents monthly.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: A portable-equipment add-on is payable only when portable oxygen is prescribed and medically necessary under Medicare coverage requirements, and it must be separately claimed to be paid.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: HCPCS codes must be used to report oxygen services, and one month of service is reported as one unit.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: For stationary oxygen prescribed at less than 1 LPM at rest, suppliers append modifier QE and the stationary monthly payment is reduced by 50 percent; HHAs use revenue code 0602.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: For stationary oxygen prescribed at greater than 4 LPM at rest, suppliers append modifier QG and the stationary monthly payment is increased by 50 percent; HHAs use revenue code 0603.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: When stationary oxygen exceeds 4 LPM at rest and portable oxygen is prescribed, suppliers append modifier QF to both the stationary and portable oxygen equipment codes; HHAs use revenue code 0604. The payment is the greater of 50 percent of the stationary monthly amount or the portable add-on fee, and no separate portable-equipment monthly payment is allowed.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: If portable oxygen was paid within the 30 days before a stationary oxygen claim billed with QG, the QG claim is returned unprocessable because the portable add-on has already been paid. If portable oxygen is billed within 30 days after a QG stationary claim, the portable claim is returned unprocessable; if both have the same date of service, both claims are returned unprocessable.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: Beginning April 1, 2018, modifier QA applies when daytime-at-rest and nighttime stationary oxygen prescriptions differ and their average is less than 1 LPM; it produces the same 50-percent reduction as QE. Modifier QR applies when the average exceeds 4 LPM and produces the same 50-percent increase as QG.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: Beginning April 1, 2018, modifier QB applies when daytime-at-rest and nighttime stationary oxygen prescriptions differ, their average exceeds 4 LPM, and portable oxygen is prescribed. QB must be used with both stationary and portable equipment codes, uses revenue code 0604 for HHAs, and does not permit a separate portable-equipment monthly payment.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: For oxygen volume-adjustment modifiers, the prescribed flow rate at rest is used when the patient's prescribed rates at rest and exercise differ. When stationary and portable flow rates differ under QF or QB, the stationary-equipment flow rate is used.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: For QF and QB, the stationary oxygen fee-schedule amount represents 100 percent of the stationary allowed amount. The portable add-on amount is the greater of 50 percent of the monthly stationary payment for the applicable stationary code or the fee-schedule amount for the portable add-on code.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: Suppliers and HHAs must indicate use of an oxygen-conserving device with an oxygen delivery system by using modifier QH.

section: 130.6 - Billing for Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment
rule_text: In states requiring licensure or certification to provide oxygen or oxygen-related products, DME MACs process claims only when the supplier has an oxygen specialty code assigned by the NSC and forwarded to the DME MAC. The specialty must meet applicable state licensing or certification requirements and state law must permit the entity to furnish the service or product.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: For a beneficiary using only a rented stationary concentrator, gaseous, or liquid system, the stationary monthly payment is billable; oxygen content fees, portable add-ons, and portable contents fees are not billable.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: For a beneficiary using only a purchased stationary system, no stationary monthly payment is billable. For purchased gaseous or liquid systems, the applicable oxygen content fee is billable; no portable add-on or portable contents fee is billable.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: When both stationary and portable systems are used and both are rented, the stationary monthly payment and portable add-on are billable, while oxygen content fees and portable contents fees are not billable.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: When the stationary system is rented and the portable system is owned, only the stationary monthly payment is billable; the portable add-on, oxygen content fee, and portable contents fee are not billable.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: When both stationary and portable systems are owned, the stationary monthly payment and portable add-on are not billable. The applicable oxygen content fee is billable for gaseous or liquid systems, and the portable contents fee is billable for a concentrator system.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: When the stationary system is owned and the portable system is rented, no stationary monthly payment is billable. The portable add-on is billable; oxygen content fees are billable for gaseous or liquid stationary systems, and portable contents fees are billable for a concentrator system.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: For a beneficiary using only a rented portable gaseous or liquid system, the portable add-on and portable contents fee are billable, while stationary monthly payment and oxygen content fee are not billable.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: For a beneficiary using only an owned portable gaseous or liquid system, only the portable contents fee is billable; the stationary monthly payment, oxygen content fee, and portable add-on are not billable.

section: 130.6.1 - Oxygen Equipment and Contents Billing Chart
rule_text: HHAs may use revenue codes 0601, 0602, 0603, and 0604 when billing oxygen under the situations in the oxygen billing chart.

section: 130.7 - Billing for Maintenance and Servicing (Providers and Suppliers)
rule_text: Maintenance and servicing are not payable while the beneficiary rents the equipment because those services are included in rental payments. The exception is the six-month service fee for a capped-rental item that the beneficiary has elected not to purchase.

section: 130.7 - Billing for Maintenance and Servicing (Providers and Suppliers)
rule_text: When purchase is permitted, including capped-rental equipment or equipment the beneficiary elects to purchase, reasonable and necessary maintenance and servicing may be paid for the purchased equipment.

section: 130.7 - Billing for Maintenance and Servicing (Providers and Suppliers)
rule_text: For capped-rental maintenance and servicing, suppliers bill the equipment HCPCS code with modifier MS for parts and labor not covered by a manufacturer or supplier warranty. HHAs use revenue code 0299 with the equipment HCPCS code.

section: 130.7 - Billing for Maintenance and Servicing (Providers and Suppliers)
rule_text: For non-capped-rental maintenance and servicing, suppliers bill the serviced item's HCPCS code with modifier RP for replacement or repair. HHAs use revenue code 0299 with the equipment HCPCS code.

section: 130.7 - Billing for Maintenance and Servicing (Providers and Suppliers)
rule_text: Hospitals billing the A/B MAC (A) for maintenance and servicing of prosthetics and orthotics report revenue code 0274 with HCPCS code L4205, L4210, L7500, L7510, or L7520.

section: 130.8 - Installment Payments
rule_text: For equipment purchased through installments, the total equipment price is reported on the first bill. Monthly payments equal the applicable rental fee-schedule amount and continue until the fee-schedule purchase price or actual charge, whichever is reached first.

section: 130.9 - Showing Whether Rented or Purchased
rule_text: Claims must identify whether equipment is rented or purchased. A purchase claim must also identify whether the equipment is new or used.

section: 130.9 - Showing Whether Rented or Purchased
rule_text: If an assigned purchase claim does not identify whether the equipment is new or used, the MAC assumes it is used and pays using the used-purchase fee. If an unassigned purchase claim lacks this information, the MAC develops the claim with the supplier.

section: 130.9 - Showing Whether Rented or Purchased
rule_text: Modifier BP indicates that the beneficiary was informed of purchase and rental options and elected to purchase; BR indicates that the beneficiary elected to rent; BU indicates that after 30 days the beneficiary had not informed the supplier of a decision.

section: 130.9 - Showing Whether Rented or Purchased
rule_text: Modifier KH identifies the initial claim or first rental month, KI identifies the second or third rental month, and KJ identifies months four through fifteen for capped rental items or PEN pumps.

section: 130.9 - Showing Whether Rented or Purchased
rule_text: Modifier NR identifies equipment that was new when rented and was subsequently purchased; NU identifies new equipment; RR identifies equipment being rented; and UE identifies used DME. For claims submitted on or after October 1, 2018, KH is no longer required with purchased claims using NU, and KH is no longer required to identify used equipment when UE is reported.

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: Supplies and drugs necessary for the effective use of DME must be billed with the appropriate HCPCS code identifying the supply. HHAs must also report revenue code 0294, Supplies/Drugs for DME Effectiveness.

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: Suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill supplies and non-implanted-DME drugs necessary for effective DME use to the DME MAC; HHAs bill the A/B MAC (HHH). Drugs necessary for effective use of implanted DME coded E0751, E0753, E0782, or E0783 are billed by non-HHAs to the A/B MAC (B), while HHAs bill the A/B MAC (HHH).

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: DME MACs must accept NDC codes for drugs billed in NCPDP format, accept NDC codes for oral anticancer drugs in professional 837, NCPDP, and CMS-1500 formats, and accept HCPCS codes for other drugs in professional 837 and CMS-1500 formats. Claims with an invalid NDC must be returned as unprocessable.

section: 140.1.1 - Supplier Payment Under Medicare Part B for Insulin Furnished Through Durable Medical Equipment
rule_text: Beginning July 1, 2023, the Part B deductible is waived for insulin furnished through covered DME, beneficiary coinsurance for a month's supply may not exceed $35, and the supplier payment must be adjusted so Medicare pays the balance for the month's supply.

section: 140.1.1 - Supplier Payment Under Medicare Part B for Insulin Furnished Through Durable Medical Equipment
rule_text: Effective July 1, 2023, every claim for insulin administered through DME must include a modifier identifying whether the supply is for one month or three months. Claims lacking one of the required supply-duration modifiers are returned to the supplier as unprocessable.

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: Suppliers and providers must bill medically necessary supplies and drugs used for the effective use of DME using the appropriate HCPCS code. HHAs must also report revenue code 0294, Supplies/Drugs for DME Effectiveness.

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: Suppliers and providers other than HHAs bill supplies and non-implanted-DME-related drugs to the DME MACs; HHAs bill these items to the A/B MAC (HHH).

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: Suppliers and providers other than HHAs must bill drugs necessary for the effective use of implanted DME associated with HCPCS E0751, E0753, E0782, or E0783 to A/B MAC (B); HHAs bill them to A/B MAC (HHH).

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: DME MACs must accept NDC codes for drugs billed in NCPDP format and for oral anticancer drugs billed in ASC X12 837 professional, NCPDP, or paper CMS-1500 formats. They must accept HCPCS codes for other drugs billed in ASC X12 837 professional or paper CMS-1500 formats.

section: 140.1 - Billing for Supplies and Drugs Related to the Effective Use of DME
rule_text: Claims containing an invalid NDC must be returned as unprocessable with the appropriate Remittance Advice Remark Code.

section: 140.1.1 - Supplier Payment Under Medicare Part B for Insulin Furnished Through DME
rule_text: Beginning July 1, 2023, the Part B deductible is waived for insulin furnished through covered DME, beneficiary coinsurance for a month's supply may not exceed $35, and supplier payment must be adjusted so Medicare pays the remainder of the month's supply amount.

section: 140.1.1 - Supplier Payment Under Medicare Part B for Insulin Furnished Through DME
rule_text: For insulin administered through DME, every claim must include modifier JK for a one-month-or-less supply or modifier JL for a three-month supply. Claims without one of these modifiers are returned as unprocessable.

section: 140.2 - Billing for HHA Medical Supplies
rule_text: HHA medical supplies are classified as routine supplies used in small quantities during usual home visits or nonroutine supplies needed for a patient's specific illness or injury under the physician's plan of care.

section: 140.2 - Billing for HHA Medical Supplies
rule_text: Routine and nonroutine medical supplies are included in the home health PPS rate and are not separately payable when the beneficiary is under a home health plan of care. If no plan of care is in place, nonroutine supplies are reported separately and are payable on 34X bills.

section: 150 - Institutional Provider Reporting of Service Units for DME and Supplies
rule_text: Provider outpatient departments must report the number of items billed for orthotic and prosthetic devices on the ASC X12 837 institutional claim or CMS-1450.

section: 150 - Institutional Provider Reporting of Service Units for DME and Supplies
rule_text: For purchased DMEPOS items, excluding frequently and substantially serviced items, capped rental items, and oxygen, HHAs report the number of purchased items as service units. For rental DME, including oxygen equipment, HHAs report one separate claim line for each month with one service unit.

section: 150 - Institutional Provider Reporting of Service Units for DME and Supplies
rule_text: For oxygen contents coded E0441, E0442, E0443, or E0444, HHAs must report the number of feet or pounds specified by the HCPCS code.

section: 160 - Billing for Total Parenteral Nutrition and Enteral Nutrition
rule_text: Providers and suppliers billing Part B parenteral or enteral nutrition as a prosthetic device benefit must bill the DME MAC. Medicare pays no more than a one-month supply for any prospective billing period, although retroactive claims may include multiple months.

section: 160.1 - Billing for TPN and EN Furnished to Part B Inpatients
rule_text: TPN and EN systems are included in inpatient Part A hospital or SNF care. If Part A benefits are not payable and coverage criteria are met, the systems, supplies, and nutrients are covered under Part B as prosthetic devices, but DME reimbursement rules continue to apply.

section: 160.1 - Billing for TPN and EN Furnished to Part B Inpatients
rule_text: Facilities furnishing covered Part B TPN or EN prosthetic devices to inpatients whose care is not covered by Part A must bill a DME MAC. HHAs, SNFs, and hospitals furnishing these items must use the ASC X12 837 professional format or, when permitted, CMS-1500; the DME MAC is selected based on the beneficiary's residence.

section: 160.1 - Billing for TPN and EN Furnished to Part B Inpatients
rule_text: A/B MACs (A) and (HHH) must return Part B PEN claims on bill types 12X, 13X, 22X, 23X, 32X, 33X, or 34X and instruct the provider to bill the DME MAC.

section: 160.2 - Special Considerations for SNF Billing for TPN and EN Under Part B
rule_text: SNFs billing Part B TPN or EN must include the HCPCS code and any applicable modifiers and bill the DME MAC using the ASC X12 837 professional format or, when applicable, CMS-1500.

section: 160.2 - Special Considerations for SNF Billing for TPN and EN Under Part B
rule_text: PEN items supplied to beneficiaries under Part A are included on the SNF Part A bill, and SNF personnel costs for administering PEN are routine Part A services and are not payable under the Part B prosthetic-device benefit.

section: 160.2 - Special Considerations for SNF Billing for TPN and EN Under Part B
rule_text: When a Part A stay is not covered and TPN qualifies as a prosthetic device, Part B covers it regardless of whether the SNF or an outside supplier furnished it; the Part B bill must be sent to the DME MAC.

section: 160.2 - Special Considerations for SNF Billing for TPN and EN Under Part B
rule_text: Enteral nutrients during a covered Part A SNF stay are treated as food and included in the routine Part A payment. Parenteral nutrient solutions during that stay are treated as intravenous drugs and must be billed by the SNF as ancillary charges.

section: 170 - Billing for Splints and Casts
rule_text: Supplies used to create casts and splints are not included in the payment amounts for fracture-management or cast/splint CPT codes. In settings using CPT payment, the supplies may be billed separately with the applicable HCPCS codes, while the work and practice expense of creating the cast or splint remain included in the service payment.

section: 170 - Billing for Splints and Casts
rule_text: For dates of service on or after July 1, 2001, A/B MAC (B) has jurisdiction over splint and cast claims, including splint codes previously billed to DME MACs.

section: 170 - Billing for Splints and Casts
rule_text: Jurisdiction for slings is shared by A/B MAC (B) for physician claims and the DME MACs for supplier claims. Hospital outpatient and hospital inpatient Part B sling services are included in OPPS payment and are billed to A/B MAC (A) on an institutional claim.

section: 170 - Billing for Splints and Casts
rule_text: Providers and suppliers that ordinarily bill A/B MAC (A) for services must bill A/B MAC (B) for splints and casts, subject to the stated hospital outpatient and inpatient Part B exception.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: From January 1, 2019 until implementation of the full home infusion therapy benefit, eligible home infusion suppliers—licensed pharmacies providing external infusion pumps and supplies—may receive separate temporary transitional payments for professional HIT services furnished in the beneficiary's home on infusion-drug administration days.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: Temporary HIT payment categories are determined by the HCPCS J-code for the home infusion drug. The DME MAC maintains the list of drugs administered through DME, and determines the category for subsequent LCD drug additions and compounded drugs coded J7799 or J7999.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: Only one HIT payment unit is made for services furnished in the beneficiary's home during an infusion-drug administration calendar day.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: Suppliers must report G0068 for specified anti-infective, pain-management, chelation, pulmonary-hypertension, or inotropic drugs; G0069 for subcutaneous immunotherapy; and G0070 for chemotherapy. Each code is reported for each infusion-drug administration day in the home and is defined in 15-minute increments.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: When multiple drugs administered on the same calendar day fall into different payment categories, only one payment is made, equal to the highest applicable category.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: Providers report visit length in 15-minute units using the specified rounding schedule: one unit for less than 23 minutes, two units for 23 to less than 38 minutes, and each subsequent unit according to the published 15-minute rounding intervals.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: Claims containing HIT G-codes may, but are not required to, also report the infusion-drug J-code, the external infusion-pump E-code, and A-codes for nondrug supplies.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: A HIT professional-services claim is subject to a CWF edit if the applicable transitional-drug J-code is absent from the same claim and from claims history for the preceding 30 days. The claim may recycle three times for a total of 15 business days and is denied if no applicable J-code claim is found.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: The appropriate drug must be billed on the same claim as the visit or no more than 30 days before it; visits are denied when the associated drug is not billed.

section: 180 - Billing for Home Infusion Therapy Services
rule_text: If multiple HIT visits occur on the same date of service, the supplier must bill only one visit and report the highest-paying visit with the applicable drug. Multiple visits reported for the same line-item date of service are returned as unprocessable.

section: 181 - Lymphedema Compression Treatment Benefit
rule_text: For items furnished on or after January 1, 2024, standard and custom-fitted compression garments and other lymphedema compression treatment items prescribed by an authorized practitioner are covered under the Medicare DMEPOS lymphedema benefit.

section: 181 - Lymphedema Compression Treatment Benefit
rule_text: Claims for lymphedema treatment items without an appropriate lymphedema diagnosis are denied. Medicare may pay for items for multiple body areas and for both a daytime and nighttime garment for the same body area.

section: 181 - Lymphedema Compression Treatment Benefit
rule_text: The allowed quantity is three daytime garments or wraps and two nighttime garments per body area. Amounts exceeding these limits are denied unless replacement is needed because of changed medical need or because the item was lost, stolen, or irreparably damaged.

section: 181 - Lymphedema Compression Treatment Benefit
rule_text: Replacement is limited to once every six months for a daytime garment or wrap and once every two years for a nighttime garment. Replacement claims must include modifier RA.

section: 181.1 - Payment Policy for Lymphedema Compression Treatment Items
rule_text: Lymphedema compression treatment items are paid in a lump sum, including garments, wraps, necessary accessories, compression bandaging supplies, and other covered treatment items.

section: 181.1 - Payment Policy for Lymphedema Compression Treatment Items
rule_text: Payment is based on 80 percent of the lesser of the supplier's actual charge or the national Medicare allowed amount for the item. National allowed amounts are updated annually.

section: 181.1 - Payment Policy for Lymphedema Compression Treatment Items
rule_text: When a new item code has pricing history, CMS or the DME MACs may map prior code payment amounts to the new code. Component-code payments may not exceed the original item's payment, global-code payments are based on the total component payments, and combined-code payments use the allowed-service-weighted arithmetic mean of the former codes' amounts.

section: 181.1 - Payment Policy for Lymphedema Compression Treatment Items
rule_text: For a new code without pricing history, the national payment amount is established through the regulatory public-meeting process. Until then, the DME MAC may price the item claim by claim, including by considering pricing for similar items.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: For DMEPOS claims, the allowable amount is the lower of the fee schedule amount or the billed charge.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: For claims to A/B MAC (B) or a DME MAC, the unmet deductible is subtracted from the allowed amount and Medicare pays 80 percent of the remainder.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: For non-nominal-charge providers billing A/B MAC (A) or (HHH), payment is 80 percent of the lower of the actual charge or fee schedule amount after subtracting the unmet deductible. For an HHA item covered under a plan of care, the same calculation applies without a deductible.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: For a nominal-charge HHA, payment is 80 percent of the fee schedule amount after subtracting the unmet deductible; when covered under a plan of care, no deductible applies. Only HHAs may be treated as nominal-charge providers for these items and services.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: For patient liability to an HHA other than a nominal-charge HHA, use 20 percent of the lower of the actual charge or fee schedule amount after the deductible, plus the unmet deductible; no deductible applies under a plan of care. For a nominal-charge HHA, use the fee schedule amount instead of the lower-of-charge calculation.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: For patient liability to a provider other than an HHA, subtract the unmet deductible from the actual charge, apply 20 percent coinsurance to the remainder, and add the unmet deductible; coinsurance applies as applicable.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: For HHA bill types 32X and 33X, no deductible or coinsurance applies except that coinsurance applies to DME and orthotic/prosthetic claims. For bill type 34X, both deductible and coinsurance apply.

section: 190 - Application of Fee Schedule and Determination of Payments and Patient Liability for DME Claims
rule_text: If subtracting the deductible produces a negative payment amount, Medicare makes no provider payment and the negative amount is not recovered from future payments. Beneficiary liability cannot exceed the applicable charge or fee schedule amount, as illustrated for HHA claims.

section: 200 - Automatic Mailing/Delivery of DMEPOS
rule_text: A supplier or manufacturer may not automatically deliver DMEPOS unless the beneficiary, physician, or designated representative has requested additional supplies or equipment. DME MAC review of this process is performed post-pay.

section: 200 - Automatic Mailing/Delivery of DMEPOS
rule_text: The beneficiary or caregiver must specifically request refills of repetitive services or supplies before dispensing. Suppliers may not initiate a refill or automatically dispense supplies on a predetermined regular schedule.

section: 200 - Automatic Mailing/Delivery of DMEPOS
rule_text: A refill request is distinct from prescription renewal. A supplier may contact the physician to obtain a renewal, but may not mail or deliver the renewed supplies until the beneficiary or caregiver specifically requests them.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: The DMEPOS benefit generally covers items for use in the beneficiary's home, not during a Part A inpatient stay; the institution is expected to provide medically necessary DMEPOS during the covered stay.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: Medicare may make separate payment for a full month of DMEPOS when the beneficiary was at home on the claim's from date or anniversary date, including when that date is the date of discharge.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: For monthly capped-rental claims, the first claim's delivery/from date must be used as the from or anniversary date on all subsequent claims unless the anniversary-date rule is reset after an overlapping inpatient stay.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: If the beneficiary is in a covered Part A stay for the entire month, Medicare does not pay for DMEPOS for that month.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: For capped rental DME, if a covered Part A stay overlaps the anniversary date but does not cover the entire month, the date of discharge becomes the new anniversary/from date. The supplier must submit a new claim using that date and annotate the claim to explain the changed anniversary date.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: The CWF rejects DME MAC claims for DMEPOS HCPCS codes when the date of service falls within the inpatient stay, treating all days before discharge as part of the stay. It processes a claim whose from date equals the inpatient discharge date and validates crossover eligibility using the from date only.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: The CWF identifies maintenance and servicing claims with modifier MS and permits payment for maintenance and servicing of capped-rental items when MS is present. Such maintenance and servicing claims may be paid regardless of whether the beneficiary is institutionalized or at home.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: The inpatient-related general policy applies to all DMEPOS paid by DME MACs, but the anniversary-date change applies only to capped-rental DME.

section: 210 - CWF Crossover Editing for DMEPOS Claims During an Inpatient Stay
rule_text: When an anniversary date falls on a calendar day absent from a subsequent month, the DME MAC uses the final day of that month for the subsequent billing date.

section: 211.1 - SNF Consolidated Billing and DME Provided by DMEPOS Suppliers
rule_text: A hospital or SNF is not the beneficiary's home for the DME benefit. DME furnished for use in an SNF is not separately payable by the DME MAC during either a covered or noncovered SNF stay, because DME is not covered for use in an SNF; a SNF also may not require the beneficiary to bring home-owned or rented DME into the facility.

section: 211.2 - Partial Month Stays for Capped Rental Equipment
rule_text: For monthly capped-rental DME, the first claim's delivery/from date must remain the from or anniversary date on subsequent claims. Medicare may pay a full month when the beneficiary spends part of the month in an SNF and part at home, provided the beneficiary is at home on the from or anniversary date.

section: unlabeled (examples preceding §211.1)
rule_text: For a rented DME item, Medicare may pay for the entire rental month when the beneficiary enters a hospital during the month and is discharged before the month ends.

section: unlabeled (examples preceding §211.1)
rule_text: If the beneficiary is hospitalized on the rental anniversary date, the claim for that anniversary date may be denied. The supplier must submit a new claim dated the discharge date, which becomes the new anniversary date for subsequent billing; the supplier should annotate the claim to explain the hospitalization and anniversary-date change.

section: unlabeled (examples preceding §211.1)
rule_text: When a new anniversary date falls on a calendar day that does not exist in a later month, the subsequent claim must use the last day of that month, such as February 28 when the anniversary date is the 31st.

section: 211.1 - General Information
rule_text: A hospital or skilled nursing facility (SNF) is not considered the beneficiary’s home for purposes of the Medicare DME benefit. This home-use restriction does not apply to Part B prosthetics, orthotics, and supplies, which may be payable regardless of the setting in which they are furnished.

section: 211.1 - General Information
rule_text: DME furnished for use in an SNF during a covered Part A stay is not separately payable by the DME MAC because it is included in the SNF payment.

section: 211.1 - General Information
rule_text: DME furnished for use in an SNF during a noncovered SNF stay is also not separately payable because the Part B DME benefit does not cover DME furnished for use in an SNF.

section: 211.1 - General Information
rule_text: An SNF may not require a beneficiary to bring personally owned or rented home DME into the SNF.

section: 211.2.A - Partial Month Stays For Capped Rental Equipment: General Rule
rule_text: For capped rental DME billed monthly, the delivery date (the first claim’s from date) is the anniversary date and must be reported as the from date on all subsequent monthly claims.

section: 211.2.A - Partial Month Stays For Capped Rental Equipment: General Rule
rule_text: Medicare pays for a full month of DME when the beneficiary spends part of the month in an SNF and part at home, provided the beneficiary is at home on the claim’s from date or anniversary date.

section: 211.2.B - Policy
rule_text: If the beneficiary is at home on the from date or anniversary date, Medicare pays for the entire DME month, even when that date is the beneficiary’s SNF discharge date.

section: 211.2.B - Policy
rule_text: Medicare does not pay for a month in which the beneficiary remains in a covered Part A SNF stay for the entire month.

section: 211.2.B - Policy
rule_text: If a covered Part A SNF stay overlaps the capped-rental from or anniversary date and does not last the entire month, the discharge date becomes the new anniversary date. The supplier must submit a claim using the discharge date as the new anniversary date and should annotate the claim to document the SNF stay and date change.

section: 211.2.B - Policy
rule_text: Maintenance and servicing of capped rental items remain payable regardless of whether the beneficiary is in a covered Part A SNF stay on the maintenance or servicing date.

section: 211.2.B - Policy
rule_text: DME is payable on the date the beneficiary is discharged from a covered Part A SNF stay. Claims must be edited using the claim’s from date rather than its through date.

section: 211.2 - Note
rule_text: The partial-month payment policy applies to all DME items paid by DME MACs, but the anniversary-date billing change applies only to capped rental DME.

section: 212 - Home Health Consolidated Billing and Supplies Provided by DMEPOS Suppliers
rule_text: While a beneficiary is under a physician-authorized home health plan of care, Medicare pays covered home health items and services through the single HHA overseeing the plan, regardless of whether the HHA, an arranged provider, contractor, consultant, or another party furnished them.

section: 212 - Home Health Consolidated Billing and Supplies Provided by DMEPOS Suppliers
rule_text: Payment for items and services subject to home health consolidated billing is included in the HHA’s home health prospective payment system episode payment; DMEPOS suppliers may not separately bill those items during the HH PPS episode.

section: 212 - Home Health Consolidated Billing and Supplies Provided by DMEPOS Suppliers
rule_text: Nonroutine medical supplies are subject to home health consolidated billing. Suppliers must use the periodically published lists of nonroutine supply codes to identify services that cannot be separately billed during an HH PPS episode.

section: 212 - Home Health Consolidated Billing and Supplies Provided by DMEPOS Suppliers
rule_text: DME, including prosthetics, orthotics, and oxygen, is exempt by law from home health consolidated billing.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: Effective January 1, 2024, Medicare makes a separate bundled payment to DME suppliers for home IVIG items and services. The payment includes nursing services and supplies, including an infusion set and tubing, used for home IVIG administration by a DME supplier.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: The home IVIG items-and-services payment is made per visit for each day a nurse administers IVIG in the patient’s home. The beneficiary must have Primary Immune Deficiency Disease (PIDD), and the IVIG product must be one listed in LCD L33610.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: HCPCS Q2052 for home IVIG administration services, supplies, and accessories may be billed separately from or on the same claim as the IVIG product J-code. When billed together, Q2052 must be a separate claim line and use the same place of service as the J-code.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: When the IVIG product is mailed or delivered before administration, the Q2052 administration date of service may be no more than 30 calendar days after the product’s J-code date of service.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: No more than one Q2052 unit may be billed per claim line for a date of service.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: Each IVIG administration date must be reported on a separate Q2052 claim line, and payment is made per visit. Multiple IVIG product units may be reported on one J-code line, followed by multiple administration lines, but only one Q2052 unit is payable for each infusion date of service.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: Q2052 visit time must be reported in 15-minute units, using the specified rounding schedule: 1 unit for less than 23 minutes; 2 units for 23 to under 38 minutes; and each subsequent unit threshold increases by 15 minutes, with 10 units for 143 to under 158 minutes.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: A Q2052 claim is subject to a Common Working File edit requiring an eligible IVIG J-code on the same claim or in claims history within the preceding 30 days. If absent, the claim is recycled three times with a 30-day lookback for a total of 15 business days; it is denied if no qualifying J-code is found after that period.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: The supplier must bill an eligible J-code listed in LCD L33610 on the visit claim or no more than 30 days before the visit; the visit is denied if the associated eligible J-code is not billed.

section: 213 - Billing for Home IVIG Items and Services
rule_text: Claims reporting multiple IVIG visits on the same line item and date of service are returned as unprocessable.
